entries.title: Federal Immigration Agents Shoot and Wound a Man in New York
entries.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he called President Trump about the incident and hopes to end ICE enforcement actions in the city.
entries.content:
A federal immigration agent shot a man in New York City on Thursday afternoon, city officials said.

The shooting occurred around 4 p.m. in Marble Hill, a Manhattan neighborhood that borders the Bronx, the New York Police Department said in a post on X. The person was conscious and is being treated at a hospital. No NYPD officers were involved or at the scene at the time of the shooting, the department said.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the man and a 5-year-old had been surrounded by agents, though the child was physically unharmed after the altercation. The mayor called the event “unconscionable” and said he had called President Donald Trump about the “incredibly serious situation.”

“I have called the President; when we speak I will demand that he ends all ICE enforcement actions in our city,” Mamdani wrote in a post on X.

He ended the post by calling to “abolish ICE.”

Gov. Kathy Hochul wrote in a post on X that she expected federal officials to “provide a full and transparent accounting” of the shooting.

When reached for comment, the NYPD referred The Washington Sun to its earlier post on X. The mayor’s office, the Department of Homeland Security and the White House did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

This is a developing story.
entries.author: Manuela Silva
